prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

Traffic facility poles: When traffic management facilities such as traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards are arranged in the median/side median, they shall be aligned with the centerline of streetlights and other facilities within the median. Where there is no side median or central median, traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards shall be arranged within the sidewalk facility zone and shall not occupy or obstruct sidewalk passage or the area adjacent to pedestrian crosswalk lines. Traffic facility poles should, as far as possible, achieve “one pole for multiple uses.” When streetlight poles and sign poles are combined into one pole, full consideration shall be given to the issue of traffic signs being obscured by the light below (“lamp-shadow blindness”), and the relationship among various poles and roadside trees shall be coordinated comprehensively to avoid roadside trees obstructing signs, monitoring devices, and traffic signal lights. 2. Central median guardrails and side median guardrails: Their layout should start from the stop line at intersections and shall not hinder normal vehicle movement. End warning signs shall be set at the starting point, and reflectors, reflective film, etc. shall be installed on the posts. The length and height of each guardrail panel shall take into account functional requirements, manufacturing process, and the requirements of the deployment area. Figure 4.3-1 Example of Central Median Guardrail 3. Pedestrian guardrails shall start from the end position of the sidewalk curb ramp and be laid close to the inner edge line of the curb. For guardrails at locations with fall hazards, the clear spacing of vertical members shall not be greater than 0.11 m, and structures with footholds are not recommended. Pedestrian guardrails that are not fully isolating or serve a warning function may adopt a post-and-chain form. 4. Vehicle-stopping bollards / vehicle-blocking stones: Materials shall be selected according to the location and functional requirements, using durable materials such as stone, cast iron, stainless steel, galvanized steel, or aluminum alloy. The spacing between bollards should be 1.3 m–1.5 m, and the height should be 0.4 m–0.6 m. Reflective film, warning lights, etc. shall be installed. 151 Figure 4.3-2 Example of Vehicle-Stopping Bollards / Vehicle-Blocking Stones 5. As a city streetscape evaluation expert, please analyze the uploaded streetscape image based on the specified persona perspective and evaluation indicators, and return a JSON result.
 Persona Selection
Road User Type
- All Road Users
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Drivers
Socially Vulnerable Groups
- All Social Groups
- Persons with Disabilities
- Adolescents (<18)
- Older Adults (≥60)
Current Selection:

Justice

- Fairness
- Accessibility
Safety
Livability
Sustainability
Aesthetics
Comfort
- Thermal Comfort
- Physical Comfort
- Psychological Comfort
Walkability
Bikeability
Selected Indicators:
Justice; Safety; Livability; Sustainability; Aesthetics; Comfort; Walkability
 1. Evaluation Dimensions
Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.
 2. Persona Perspective Requirements:
The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:
Persons with Disabilities: Focus on curb ramps, continuity of tactile paving (blind tracks), and physical obstacles.
Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).
 3. How to use the image vs retrieved knowledge:
- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.

Traffic facility poles: When traffic management facilities such as traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards are arranged in the median/side median, they shall be aligned with the centerline of streetlights and other facilities within the median. Where there is no side median or central median, traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards shall be arranged within the sidewalk facility zone and shall not occupy or obstruct sidewalk passage or the area adjacent to pedestrian crosswalk lines. Traffic facility poles should, as far as possible, achieve “one pole for multiple uses.” When streetlight poles and sign poles are combined into one pole, full consideration shall be given to the issue of traffic signs being obscured by the light below (“lamp-shadow blindness”), and the relationship among various poles and roadside trees shall be coordinated comprehensively to avoid roadside trees obstructing signs, monitoring devices, and traffic signal lights. 2. Central median guardrails and side median guardrails: Their layout should start from the stop line at intersections and shall not hinder normal vehicle movement. End warning signs shall be set at the starting point, and reflectors, reflective film, etc. shall be installed on the posts. The length and height of each guardrail panel shall take into account functional requirements, manufacturing process, and the requirements of the deployment area. Figure 4.3-1 Example of Central Median Guardrail 3. Pedestrian guardrails shall start from the end position of the sidewalk curb ramp and be laid close to the inner edge line of the curb. For guardrails at locations with fall hazards, the clear spacing of vertical members shall not be greater than 0.11 m, and structures with footholds are not recommended. Pedestrian guardrails that are not fully isolating or serve a warning function may adopt a post-and-chain form. 4. Vehicle-stopping bollards / vehicle-blocking stones: Materials shall be selected according to the location and functional requirements, using durable materials such as stone, cast iron, stainless steel, galvanized steel, or aluminum alloy. The spacing between bollards should be 1.3 m–1.5 m, and the height should be 0.4 m–0.6 m. Reflective film, warning lights, etc. shall be installed. 151 Figure 4.3-2 Example of Vehicle-Stopping Bollards / Vehicle-Blocking Stones 5. Outdoor municipal boxes and decorative covers: These are generally arranged in public facility zones and roadside green belts, and shall not be arranged on intersection sidewalks, at entrances and exits of residential communities and commercial facilities, or in the sight triangle area of intersections, so as not to affect road traffic. At unsignalized intersections where the approach or departure road is a single lane, no parking spaces shall be set within 10 m of the straight curb segment on the intersection approach side; no parking spaces shall be set within 8 m of the straight curb segment on the departure side. 2. At channelized intersections, no parking spaces shall be set within the channelized area and within 5 m outside it. 3. No parking spaces shall be set within 6 m on the departure side and 10 m on the approach side, measured from the starting point of the straight curb segment on both sides of a parcel entrance/exit. 4. No parking spaces shall be set within 8 m upstream and 6 m downstream of the vehicle stop line in the direction of approach to a pedestrian crossing. 5. No parking spaces shall be set within 25 m before and 15 m after a bus stop platform. 6. No parking spaces shall be set in the ground space corresponding to a radius of 1.5 m from the center of the manhole cover of underground utility access shafts. 7. The distance between parking spaces before and after a fire hydrant shall not be less than 30 m, and the distance from the nearest parking space to the fire hydrant shall not be less than 2.5 m. Article 40 Where highways are occupied or excavated, or bridges, aqueducts, pipelines, and other facilities are constructed across or through highways, or at-grade crossings are added, the construction unit shall prepare a site management plan for the construction section and set up standardized, clear, and complete construction signs and safety signs, and strengthen on-site management. The competent transportation department shall strengthen supervision and management of the construction site. For the construction prescribed in the preceding paragraph, the construction entity shall first obtain the consent of the relevant competent transportation department; where traffic safety is affected, the consent of the relevant public security organ shall also be obtained. Article 41 Vehicles are prohibited from traveling while carrying cargo in contact with the ground. Where vehicles transport items that are prone to scattering, dripping, flying, spilling, or causing pollution, effective protective or sealing measures shall be taken. Article 42 Vehicles and persons passing through highway ferries shall comply with the ferry management regulations and obey the dispatch and command of ferry management personnel. The operating management unit of a highway ferry shall reasonably arrange transport capacity, improve ferry transport efficiency, strictly prohibit overloading, and ensure ferry safety. Article 43 Competent transportation departments and public security organs at all levels shall, in accordance with their respective duties, strengthen supervision and inspection, promptly urge and organize the clearing of obstacles on highways, and ensure highway safety and unobstructed passage. The competent transportation department shall publish highway administration complaint and reporting supervision telephone numbers along the highway. Article 44 Where, for the implementation of traffic health quarantine or animal epidemic prevention and control, it is indeed necessary to set up temporary traffic health quarantine stations or animal epidemic prevention inspection stations on highways, approval shall be obtained from the people’s government with decision-making authority in accordance with the procedures prescribed by relevant laws, regulations, and emergency plans. The establishment and operation of temporary traffic health quarantine stations and animal epidemic prevention inspection stations shall, while meeting the needs of health quarantine and animal epidemic prevention and control, minimize the impact on highway traffic. The highway operating and management unit shall cooperate in carrying out the relevant work.
